"
A run represents a discrete unit of agent work. One session contains many runs.

## Status Transitions

- `running` → `completed`: work finished successfully
- `running` → `failed`: work encountered an error
- `running` → `cancelled`: run was interrupted or abandoned

No transitions out of terminal states (completed/failed/cancelled).

## Fields

- `intent`: human-readable description of what this run is trying to do (set at start)
- `error`: raw error/exception text on failure; null otherwise
- `completed_at`: set when transitioning to any terminal status

## Commits

Agent work that modifies rows should be committed to a bundle and linked via `ai.run_commit (run_id, commit_id)`. A run may have zero or many commits.

" SELECT r.id,
    r.status,
    a.name AS agent,
    s.title AS session,
    r.intent,
    r.started_at,
    r.completed_at,
        CASE
            WHEN (r.status = 'running'::ai.run_status) THEN ('running '::text || to_char(make_interval(secs => ((EXTRACT(epoch FROM (now() - r.started_at)))::integer)::double precision), 'MI"m" SS"s"'::text))
            WHEN (r.completed_at IS NOT NULL) THEN TRIM(BOTH FROM to_char(make_interval(secs => ((EXTRACT(epoch FROM (r.completed_at - r.started_at)))::integer)::double precision), 'MI"m" SS"s"'::text))
            ELSE NULL::text
        END AS duration,
    count(DISTINCT rc.commit_id) AS commit_count,
    COALESCE(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('bundle', repo.name, 'message', c.message, 'commit_id', c.id) ORDER BY c.commit_time) FILTER (WHERE (c.id IS NOT NULL)), '[]'::jsonb) AS commits,
    r.error
   FROM (((((ai.run r
     JOIN ai.session s ON ((s.id = r.session_id)))
     JOIN ai.agent a ON ((a.id = s.agent_id)))
     LEFT JOIN ai.run_commit rc ON ((rc.run_id = r.id)))
     LEFT JOIN bundle.commit c ON ((c.id = rc.commit_id)))
     LEFT JOIN bundle.repository repo ON ((repo.id = c.repository_id)))
  GROUP BY r.id, r.status, a.name, s.title, r.intent, r.started_at, r.completed_at, r.error
  ORDER BY r.started_at DESC;"

"
Convenience view joining `ai.run`, `ai.session`, and `ai.agent` with computed fields.

## Key Columns

- `duration`: human-readable elapsed time — `"07m 19s"` for completed runs, `"running 03m 12s"` for in-flight
- `commit_count`: number of bundle commits linked to this run
- `commits`: jsonb array of commit summaries, shape:
  ```json
  [
    { "bundle": "org.aquameta.core.widget", "message": "edit bootscreen", "commit_id": "01872c32-..." }
  ]
  ```
  Empty array `[]` when no commits.

## Usage

Intended as the primary observability surface for agent activity. The `ai_run_summary` widget renders this view at `/ai/runs`.

"
A session is a continuous working context for an agent. Sessions group related runs.

## context jsonb

Free-form configuration and state. Recommended keys:

- `model` (text): Claude model ID in use, e.g. `"claude-sonnet-4-6"`. Should match `ai.agent.model` unless overriding per-session.

Other keys are not yet standardized — document them here as usage patterns emerge.

## Lifecycle

Sessions do not have a status field. Use `ended_at` to mark completion (null = active).
"

"
## Purpose

This bundle provides the schema for tracking AI agent activity in Aquameta. Every agent action is recorded as rows in the `ai` schema, giving the system full provenance over what agents did, when, and with what effect.

## Core Concepts

**Agent**: A named, configured AI participant (model + capabilities). Agents are instance-specific — they are not shipped in this bundle. Create one with `INSERT INTO ai.agent (name, model)`.

**Session**: A continuous working context for an agent. One agent may have many sessions over time. Sessions carry a `context` jsonb field for configuration and state.

**Run**: A discrete unit of agent work within a session. An agent creates a run at the start of a task, sets its `intent`, and updates `status` when done. Runs can produce commits (via `ai.run_commit`) which link agent work to bundle version history.

## Agent Loop

1. Create or resume a session: `INSERT INTO ai.session (agent_id, title, context)`
2. Create a run: `INSERT INTO ai.run (session_id, intent)`
3. Do work (edit rows via PGFS, SQL, or REST API)
4. Stage and commit affected bundles
5. Record commits: `INSERT INTO ai.run_commit (run_id, commit_id)`
6. Mark run done: `UPDATE ai.run SET status = 'completed', completed_at = now() WHERE id = ...`

On failure: set `status = 'failed'`, write the raw error to `error`.
On cancellation (stale/interrupted): set `status = 'cancelled'`.

## What Belongs in the Bundle

Schema (tables, views, functions, types) belongs in `extensions/ai/000-ai.sql` and is re-run on fresh installs. The bundle ships row data: capabilities, widget, resource page, documentation. Operational data (sessions, runs, messages) is instance-specific and is NOT tracked.

## Interfaces

All four Aquameta interfaces write to the same rows:
- SQL/psql: direct INSERT/UPDATE
- PGFS: write to `pgfs/<schema>/<table>/<uuid>/<column>`
- REST API: PATCH `/endpoint/0.3/ai/run/<uuid>`
- Web IDE: widget editor or raw table view
"
